financials.source: Emory University Form 990 (EIN 58-0566256, FYE August 31, 2024) and FY2024 Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. Note: EIN is Emory University consolidated, which includes Emory Healthcare. Operating income figure is the 990 surplus (total revenue minus total expenses) and includes $763.9M in investment income; excluding investment returns, the consolidated entity would show an operating deficit.

balanceSheetWealth.investmentPortfolioSource: Emory University FY2024 consolidated financial statements — total investments across all asset classes
balanceSheetWealth.realEstateSource: Not separately disclosed in consolidated financials
balanceSheetWealth.notes: Emory Investment Management oversees $13.1B+ in diversified investments for Emory University, Emory Healthcare, and The Carter Center. 54% allocated to alternatives including private equity, venture capital, real estate, natural resources, and absolute return strategies. Approximately 40% of endowment dedicated to health care and health sciences. Endowment distributes approximately 5% of value annually to support operations.

bondDebt.largestIssue: Georgia Private Colleges and Universities Authority Revenue Bonds, 2025 Series
bondDebt.largestIssueProceeds: $2.1B authorized by Georgia; $486M first tranche marketed May 2025 at rates of 5% or less
bondDebt.issuerAuthority: Georgia Private Colleges and Universities Authority
bondDebt.source: Emory University FY2024 Audited Consolidated Financial Statements (total bonds and notes payable including unamortized net premium); Bloomberg and SaportaReport for 2025 issuance details. Moody's rated the 2025 bonds at Aa2.

executiveComp.source: Form 990 Schedule J (EIN 58-0566256, FYE August 2024): Joon S. Lee MD received $2,494,860 from reporting organization, $0 from related organizations, $320,856 estimated other compensation. Georgia HB321 compensation report lists $2,860,918 total. Highest-compensated officer at Emory University overall is Ravi Thadhani MD MPH at $5.1M; 47 individuals reported on Schedule J.

communityBenefit.source: Emory Healthcare FY2024 Community Benefit Report ($519.5M hospitals + $59.2M non-hospitals = $578.7M total). Charity care of $151.5M from FY2024 data. Georgia state average charity care of 10.3% of expenses from Lown Hospitals Index (FY2021). Emory's charity care represents approximately 2.3% of consolidated expenses, well below the state average.

taxAdvantage.notes: Emory University is a tax-exempt 501(c)(3) organization. Bond debt of $3.3B issued through Georgia Private Colleges and Universities Authority generates significant tax-exempt interest subsidy. Multiple Emory hospitals participate in 340B program as DSH entities. Interest expense of $110.3M in FY2024 (net of $17.5M capitalized interest). Average variable rate on tax-exempt bonds was 3.54%; taxable variable bonds averaged 5.70%.

layoffs.source: Emory spokesperson told Becker's 232 positions affected out of 29,500 employees (less than 1%); class-action lawsuit filed August 15, 2025 by Paulette Simmons claims 543 full-time employees affected. Financial services and revenue cycle positions eliminated to streamline operations. WSB-TV, AJC, Becker's Hospital Review.

keyRiskFactors: Consolidated entity operationally dependent on $764M in annual investment returns to offset operating deficit
Significant capital commitments including $2.1B new bond authorization in 2025
WARN Act class-action lawsuit challenging layoff procedures
Ongoing integration of Houston Healthcare acquisition

acquisitions.description: Two hospital campuses (282 beds), five outpatient facilities, nine physician practices in Warner Robins and Perry, Georgia. 2,500 employees, 200 physicians, serving 300,000+ patients annually. LOI signed August 2024, Georgia AG approved February 2025, completed June 1, 2025.
acquisitions.source: Emory Healthcare, Kaufman Hall, Fox 5 Atlanta, Chief Healthcare Executive

legalIssues.description: Former employee Paulette Simmons filed class-action lawsuit alleging Emory Healthcare violated the federal WARN Act by laying off 543 employees without required 60-day notice. Suit claims severance agreements contained provisions barring WARN Act claims, which cannot be waived absent statutory compliance.
legalIssues.source: AJC, Black Enterprise, WSB-TV, Becker's Hospital Review

ratios.investmentsToOperatingIncomeInterpretati: Emory's $13.1B investment portfolio is nearly 20x its $669M annual surplus, with $764M in investment returns exceeding the surplus itself — meaning the consolidated entity would operate at a deficit without its investment portfolio.
ratios.bondDebtToCommunityBenefitInterpretation: Tax-exempt bond debt of $3.3B is 5.7x the $578.7M claimed community benefit, raising questions about the scale of public subsidy relative to community reinvestment.
ratios.charityCareVsStateInterpretation: Emory's charity care of $151.5M represents approximately 2.3% of consolidated expenses, compared to Georgia's 10.3% state average — roughly one-fifth of the state average. Note: comparison uses consolidated university expenses as denominator and state average is FY2021 data.

accusation: Emory University holds a $13.1 billion investment portfolio and an $11.4 billion endowment — balance sheet wealth exceeding that of most Fortune 500 companies — while its healthcare arm provided just $151.5 million in charity care (roughly 2.3% of expenses, far below Georgia's 10.3% state average), carries $3.3 billion in tax-exempt bond debt, laid off hundreds of workers in 2025 triggering a WARN Act class-action lawsuit, and serves as the Atlanta Falcons' official healthcare partner, all under the shelter of its tax-exempt nonprofit status.
